edges.description: Missense alleles at R116 and in the N-terminal region reduce chaperone activity of the mutant subunits.
Mutant subunits form polydisperse or abnormally sized oligomers and exchange subunits poorly.
R49C, unlike wild-type alphaA-crystallin, mislocalizes to the nucleus and does not protect lens epithelial cells from apoptosis.
Dominant alleles, particularly at R116, are associated with microcornea and other anterior segment malformation; the developmental mechanism is not established.
Absence of alphaA-crystallin removes its chaperone contribution, and alphaB-crystallin becomes insoluble without it.
Microcornea accompanies the recessive R54C cataract; its cause is hypothesized.

nodes.description: Native alpha-crystallin is a large, dynamic heteropolymer of alphaA and alphaB subunits. R116C and R116H oligomers are much larger and polydisperse; R12C, R21W and R54C are moderately larger; R21Q lens material from a patient lacks the high-molecular-weight oligomer.

evidence.reference_title: Quaternary structural parameters of the congenital cataract causing mutants of αA-crystallin.
evidence.snippet: The average molar mass and mass across the peak showed major increase in R116C and R116H, moderate increase in R12C, R21W, and R54C, and no increase in R21L and R49C as compared to αA-wt.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a novel oligomerization disrupting mutation in CRYΑA associated with congenital cataract in a South Australian family.
evidence.snippet: Western blotting of proteins freshly extracted from cataractous lens material of the proband demonstrated a marked reduction in the amount of the high-molecular-weight oligomers seen in the lens material of an unaffected individual.

nodes.description: One of several morphologies within the R116H family.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical variability of autosomal dominant cataract, microcornea and corneal opacity and novel mutation in the alpha A crystallin gene (CRYAA).
evidence.snippet: Clinically, affected individuals had diverse and novel cataracts with variable morphology (anterior polar, cortical, embryonal, fan-shaped, anterior subcapsular).

evidence.reference_title: Evaluating gene-disease relationship strength in crystallin genes in association with pediatric cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Seven genes (CRYAA, CRYAB, CRYBA1, CRYBB1, CRYBB2, CRYGC, CRYGD) scored as Definitively associated with autosomal dominant (AD) inherited pediatric cataracts.

evidence.reference_title: Cell death triggered by a novel mutation in the alphaA-crystallin gene underlies autosomal dominant cataract linked to chromosome 21q.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis identified a C --> T transition in exon 1 of CRYAA from affected individuals that was predicted to result in the nonconservative substitution of cysteine for arginine at codon 49 (R49C).

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a novel oligomerization disrupting mutation in CRYΑA associated with congenital cataract in a South Australian family.
evidence.snippet: We identified a novel segregating heterozygous mutation, c.62G>A (p.R21Q), in the CRYΑA gene in one family.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a novel, putative cataract-causing allele in CRYAA (G98R) in an Indian family.
evidence.snippet: The G98R mutation segregates only in affected family members and is not seen in representative controls.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense substitutions, mostly at arginine residues in the N-terminal region (R12, R21, R49, R54) or the alpha-crystallin domain (R116), alter alphaA-crystallin structure. The effect on chaperone activity is allele-dependent: R116C and R116H lose most activity, R12C, R21L and R21W lose a moderate amount, and R49C and R54C retain normal activity against the ADH client in vitro, so reduced chaperone capacity is not the only route to disease.

evidence.reference_title: Structural and functional changes in the alpha A-crystallin R116C mutant in hereditary cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Chaperone-like activity of the alphaA R116C mutant is approximately 4-fold lower than wild type, whether measured before or after conversion to a polydisperse population with incubation.

evidence.reference_title: Quaternary structural parameters of the congenital cataract causing mutants of αA-crystallin.
evidence.snippet: Chaperone activity, as measured with ADH as the target protein, appeared normal in R49C and R54C, while R12C, R21L, and R21W showed moderate loss and R116C and R116H showed significant loss.

nodes.description: Homozygous W9X introduces a stop codon at residue 9 and is expected to abolish alphaA-crystallin; homozygous R54C is a missense allele whose carriers have subclinical punctate opacities, so heterozygous R54C is not fully silent, and R54C has elsewhere been reported as a dominant allele whose chaperone activity is normal in vitro. The loss-of-function category is therefore secure for W9X only; for R54C it is an assumption from recessive transmission. The Cryaa-null mouse, which makes no alphaA-crystallin, models complete loss.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation (W9X) in CRYAA causes autosomal recessive cataract in an inbred Jewish Persian family.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the CRYAA in this Jewish Persian family revealed a G-to-A substitution, resulting in the formation of a premature stop codon (W9X).

evidence.reference_title: Targeted disruption of the mouse alpha A-crystallin gene induces cataract and cytoplasmic inclusion bodies containing the small heat shock protein alpha B-crystallin.
evidence.snippet: Mice that are homozygous for the disrupted allele produce no detectable alpha A in their lenses, based on protein gel electrophoresis and immunoblot analysis.

nodes.description: Lens extraction for visually significant opacity, followed by optical correction and amblyopia therapy. For dense bilateral congenital cataract the timing of surgery in the first weeks of life governs visual outcome. The timing evidence comes from cohorts that were not genotyped. No CRYAA-specific therapy exists.

evidence.reference_title: The critical period for surgical treatment of dense congenital bilateral cataracts.
evidence.snippet: During weeks 0-14, mean visual acuity decreased by 1 line with each 3 weeks' delay in surgery.

nodes.description: Lens opacity present at birth or in infancy, the usual presentation of both forms; congenital total white cataract in the recessive R54C sibship.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant congenital cataract associated with a missense mutation in the human alpha crystallin gene CRYAA.
evidence.snippet: We have mapped an ADCC gene in family ADCC-2 to chromosome 21q22.3 near the alpha-crystallin gene CRYAA.

evidence.reference_title: Recessive congenital total cataract with microcornea and heterozygote carrier signs caused by a novel missense CRYAA mutation (R54C).
evidence.snippet: Three siblings had congenital total white cataract with microcornea; the parents and seven other siblings were asymptomatic.

evidence.snippet: The alphaA-R49C heterozygous and homozygous knock-in lenses demonstrated an increase in insoluble alphaA-crystallin and alphaB-crystallin and a surprising increase in expression of cytoplasmic gamma-crystallin, whereas no changes in beta-crystallin were observed.

evidence.snippet: Light and transmission electron microscopy reveal the presence of dense inclusion bodies in the central lens fiber cells.

nodes.description: Microcornea, corneal opacity and other anterior segment anomalies accompany CRYAA cataract in some families. Whether they arise from an inductive effect of the abnormal lens or from loss of alphaA-crystallin in the developing cornea is unknown.

evidence.snippet: The CCMC phenotype demonstrates variable expression with regard to cataract morphology and age of appearance.

evidence.snippet: With the exception of iris coloboma, the clinical features in all six previously reported families with mutations in the CRYAA gene were found in this family.

nodes.description: Lens fiber cells cannot turn over proteins, so the alpha-crystallins, as holdase chaperones, sequester destabilized beta- and gamma-crystallins and keep them soluble. Reduced or absent alphaA-crystallin activity lowers this capacity.

biological_processes: chaperone-mediated maintenance of lens protein solubility

evidence.reference_title: Transgenic zebrafish models reveal distinct molecular mechanisms for cataract-linked αA-crystallin mutants.
evidence.snippet: Terminally differentiated lens fiber cells, devoid of cellular machineries that repair and turn proteins over, rely on two small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), αA- and αB-crystallin, which function as molecular chaperones by sequestering thermodynamically destabilized client proteins to inhibit aggregation [2–5].
